pr.title: Remove fake borrows of refs that are converted into non-refs in `MakeByMoveBody`
pr.author: compiler-errors

issues.title: by_move_body.rs:275:21: There should be at least a single deref for an upvar local initialization, found []
issues.body:
### Code This compiler error appeared when I tried to wrap my function in an async block so I could use inner returns without returning from the parent fn; I want to call `.wrap_err` from `eyre` crate on whatever is returning so I can attach some information. I had previously attempted to use the unstable `try_blocks` feature, but I think my `return Err` and `bail!` usage in the body was returning from the fn instead of the try block. removing the wrapping async closure fixes the rustc-ice compiler error. https://github.com/AAFC-Cloud/Cloud-Terrastodon/commit/fc55eb875a6869e4cb7ceb1dc38e20f2c4ba6664 ```diff diff --git a/rust/crates/command/src/command.rs b/rust/crates/command/src/command.rs index 10f645d..9c52993 100644 --- a/rust/crates/command/src/command.rs +++ b/rust/crates/command/src/command.rs @@ -550,7 +550,7 @@ impl CommandBuilder { #[async_recursion] #[track_caller] pub async fn run_raw(&self) -> Result { - let result: eyre::Result = (async ||{ + // let result: eyre::Result = (async ||{ // Check cache match self.get_cached_output().await { Ok(None) => {} @@ -685,10 +685,10 @@ impl CommandBuilder { // Return success Ok(output) - })().await; - result - .wrap_err(format!("Invoking command `{}`", self.summarize())) - .wrap_err(format!("Called from {}", std::panic::Location::caller())) + // })().await; + // result + // .wrap_err(format!("Invoking command `{}`", self.summarize())) + // .wrap_err(format!("Called from {}", std::panic::Location::caller())) } pub async fn run(&self) -> Result ``` here is the permalink to the relevant file at the commit where the compiler error manifests https://github.com/AAFC-Cloud/Cloud-Terrastodon/blob/73709d3861d008195bb14824e1fc1bb0f03c1940/rust/crates/command/src/command.rs#L553 ``` cd cloud_terrastodon/rust cargo build ``` [rustc-ice-2025-03-14T14_54_32-34820.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19249551/rustc-ice-2025-03-14T14_54_32-34820.txt) ### Meta `rustc --version --verbose`: ``` rustc 1.87.0-nightly (f8a913b13 2025-02-23) binary: rustc commit-hash: f8a913b1381e90379c7ca63ac2b88b9518936628 commit-date: 2025-02-23 host: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc release: 1.87.0-nightly LLVM version: 20.1.0 ``` ### Error output ``` cargo build 2>&1 | set-clipboard ```

--- I tried getting a smaller reproduction but was unsuccessful. The following code builds and runs without errors.
This compiles and runs properly ```rust use eyre::Context; #[tokio::main] async fn main() -> eyre::Result<()> { println!("Hello, world!"); let bruh = Bruh { name: "hehe".to_string(), }; // Call once; if it recurses, you might see the ICE. bruh.bruh().await?; Ok(()) } struct Bruh { pub name: String, } impl Bruh { #[async_recursion::async_recursion] #[track_caller] pub async fn bruh(&self) -> eyre::Result { let result: eyre::Result = (async || { println!("Level 1: {}", self.name); // Nest a second async closure: let inner = async || { println!("Level 2: {}", self.name); // Nest a third async closure: let inner_most = async || { println!("Level 3: {}", self.name); Ok(1) }; inner_most().await }; inner().await })() .await; result.wrap_err(format!("Called from {}", std::panic::Location::caller())) } } /* [dependencies] async-recursion = "1.1.1" eyre = "0.6.12" tokio = { version = "1.44.1", features = ["full"] } */ ```

analysis.summary: Confirmed bug fix in MakeByMoveBody (StateTransform): when the by-move body replaces a child capture of type `&Foo` with an owned by-move capture `Foo` (field remapping has `peel_deref == true`), the pass must also replace a direct fake shallow borrow of that upvar (`_N = &fake shallow (_1.field)`) with `nop`. Leaving/visiting that obsolete fake borrow is the historically incorrect behavior and is associated with the reported ICE `by_move_body.rs:275:21: There should be at least a single deref for an upvar local initialization, found []` (Fixes #138501). Fake borrows that go through a deref, or fields not converted ref->non-ref, are not removed.
analysis.originalLogic: Before the fix, `MakeByMoveBody` overrode `visit_place` (to rewrite child capture places to the by-move versions) and `visit_local_decl` (to replace the type of `ty::CAPTURE_STRUCT_LOCAL` with `self.by_move_coroutine_ty`), but it did not override `visit_statement`. Consequently fake shallow borrow statements of child capture fields were traversed like any other statement and were retained. For a child capture that was remapped with `peel_deref == true` (child capture `&Foo` becoming owned `Foo` in the by-move body), the direct fake borrow of the upvar, e.g. `_5 = &fake shallow (_1.0: &Foo)`, remained in the child body even though `_1.0` no longer has type `&Foo`. Visit of that place is also on the path that panicked with the reported upvar-initialization deref assertion.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically wrong by-move-body transformation kept the obsolete fake shallow borrow of the directly projected capture field after that field had been converted from a reference capture (`_1.0: &Foo`) into a by-move owned capture (`_1.0: Foo`). In the supplied child MIR, the corrected output has `nop;` in the position where the pre-fix logic would retain the direct fake borrow `_5 = &fake shallow (_1.0: &Foo)`. A separate agent can model the wrong transformation by not filtering that statement (or by visiting its place as an upvar initialization), while the correct transformation sets `statement.kind = mir::StatementKind::Nop` only when the place is exactly `CAPTURE_STRUCT_LOCAL.Field(idx, _)` and the remapped field has `peel_deref == true`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust programs using async closures / coroutine closures (`async move || { ... }`) where the parent capture owns a value (`Foo`) and the child capture is a reference (`&Foo`), and the body contains a `match` (here with a guard) that causes MIR borrowck to emit fake shallow borrows of the capture. The supplied regression source is: `fn foo(f: &Foo) { let x = async move || match f { Foo::Bar if true => {} _ => {} }; }` with `enum Foo { Bar, Baz }`. The direct-field fake borrow is the one without a deref; fake borrows through derefs such as `&fake shallow (*(_1.0: &Foo))` remain.
analysis.trigger: The by-move body contains a `StatementKind::Assign` whose rvalue is `Rvalue::Ref(_, BorrowKind::Fake(FakeBorrowKind::Shallow), place)`, where `place.as_ref()` is `PlaceRef { local: ty::CAPTURE_STRUCT_LOCAL, projection: [ProjectionElem::Field(idx, _)] }` and `self.field_remapping.get(&idx)` is `Some(&(_, _, true, _))` (the `peel_deref` flag is true).
preconditions: The `MakeByMoveBody` transform is constructing the by-move (`AsyncFnOnce`) coroutine body for an async closure / coroutine-closure pair.
The capture field is remapped with `peel_deref == true`, i.e. the child capture is a reference (`&Foo`) while the by-move body owns the value (`Foo`).
The child MIR has a fake shallow borrow whose place is exactly the capture-struct local plus a single Field projection (no deref), typically emitted for a match guard / matched place.
`field_remapping` has an entry for that child field index and its third tuple element (the `peel_deref` flag) is true.
pitfalls: Only nop the fake borrow when the projection is exactly a single `Field` on `ty::CAPTURE_STRUCT_LOCAL`; fake borrows with a deref, e.g. `&fake shallow (*(_1.0))`, must not be removed by this rule.
The third tuple element must be checked: if `peel_deref` is false, the capture was not converted from a reference to a by-move value, so a direct fake borrow of the upvar is not necessarily obsolete.
After changing the statement to `StatementKind::Nop`, still call `self.super_statement(statement, location)` to preserve normal traversal.
The patch also adds `self.super_local_decl(local, local_decl)` after retyping the capture local; omitting it changes which nested declarations/places are visited.
Fake borrows are MIR borrowck artifacts and the by-move body does not need borrowck, but the intended behavior is still to preserve non-obsolete fake borrows rather than remove all of them.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a MIR-opt regression test (as in the patch) with `//@ edition:2021` and `// skip-filecheck`, defining `enum Foo { Bar, Baz }` and `fn foo(f: &Foo) { let x = async move || match f { Foo::Bar if true => {} _ => {} }; }`, then emit both the parent coroutine and the by-move child MIR via `// EMIT_MIR ...built.after.mir`. In the expected child MIR, assert that the direct fake shallow borrow of the capture field became `nop;` while the deref fake borrows remain (`_3 = &fake shallow (*(_1.0: &Foo)); _4 = &fake shallow (_1.0: &Foo); nop;` in the supplied expectation). As a control, construct an input where the capture is not peeled from reference to by-value, or where the fake borrow includes a deref, and verify the direct-field nop rule does not apply. This also serves as an ICE regression: without the fix the reported panic is `There should be at least a single deref for an upvar local initialization, found []`.
evidence: Remove fake borrows of closure captures if that capture has been replaced with a by-move version of that capture.
we never have an upvar of type `&Foo`, and we should replace it with a `nop`.
Remove fake borrows of refs that are converted into non-refs in `MakeByMoveBody`
